entities.summary:
Juan Castellar y de Borja (1441–1505) was a Spanish Roman Catholic bishop and cardinal who played a significant role in the Council of Pisa, where he advocated for the rights of the clergy. He was appointed as the Bishop of Béziers by Pope Alexander VI in 1492, a position he held until his death in 1505. His influence extended to the appointment of several high-ranking officials, including the Bishop of Carthage and the Archbishop of Palermo.

Castellar y de Borja was also involved in the transfer of wealth from the Spanish crown to the Catholic Church, which had significant economic implications for both parties. The cardinal's efforts were instrumental in securing a substantial portion of the tax revenue generated by the conquest of Granada in 1492.

Despite his influential role, Castellar y de Borja's legacy remains somewhat overshadowed by that of other prominent figures of the time. Nonetheless, his contributions to the Church and his impact on the political landscape of Spain during the late 15th century cannot be overstated.
